root_cause.text: The buffer sampling frequency sysfs attribute was unconditionally created for all sensor types, but the underlying `st_lsm6dsx_hwfifo_odr_store()` function only supports accelerometer and gyroscope by accessing a 2-entry `odr_table` array indexed by `sensor->id`, causing out-of-bounds access when other sensor types (with higher IDs) attempt to write this attribute.
root_cause.evidence: The patch conditionally assigns `st_lsm6dsx_buffer_attrs` (which contains the buffer sampling frequency attribute) only when `i == ST_LSM6DSX_ID_ACC`, replacing the unconditional assignment that previously passed `st_lsm6dsx_buffer_attrs` for all sensor types. The CVE description explicitly states that `odr_table` is "only 2 entries long" and that "an access for any sensor type other than accelerometer or gyroscope is an out-of-bounds access," confirming the mismatch between attribute availability and the function's supported sensor types.

intent_record.intent_summary: Enable accelerometer-specific FIFO sampling frequency configuration independent of sensor sampling rate to support accurate high-rate event detection while maintaining low FIFO data rates.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional variable `attrs` that selects between `st_lsm6dsx_buffer_attrs` for accelerometer devices (ST_LSM6DSX_ID_ACC) and NULL for others, then passed this variable to `devm_iio_kfifo_buffer_setup_ext()` instead of always passing `st_lsm6dsx_buffer_attrs`. Also added an explanatory comment describing the rationale for accelerometer-specific FIFO sampling frequency configuration.
intent_record.how: This change makes FIFO buffer attribute setup conditional based on device type. For accelerometer devices, the full set of buffer attributes (including FIFO sampling frequency controls) are applied, allowing independent FIFO data rate configuration. For other sensor types (gyroscope, etc.), no custom attributes are applied (NULL), preventing them from having separate FIFO frequency settings. This enables the accelerometer to maintain high sensor sampling rates while keeping FIFO data rates low for efficient event detection.

grouping_result.intent: Enable accelerometer-specific FIFO sampling frequency configuration independent of sensor sampling rate to support accurate high-rate event detection while maintaining low FIFO data rates.

relevance_review.reason: The group's intent is to enable accelerometer-specific FIFO sampling frequency configuration as a feature enhancement. The vulnerability root cause is about preventing out-of-bounds array access by restricting the sysfs attribute to only supported sensor types (accelerometer and gyroscope). These are fundamentally different issues - one is adding functionality, the other is fixing a safety bug by limiting attribute exposure. The group does not address the core vulnerability of unconditional attribute creation for unsupported sensor types.

candidates.rationale: This statement unconditionally registers buffer attributes (st_lsm6dsx_buffer_attrs) for all sensor types (i from 0 to ST_LSM6DSX_ID_MAX). The attributes include the hwfifo_odr sysfs attribute which calls st_lsm6dsx_hwfifo_odr_store(). This function only supports accelerometer and gyroscope (2-entry odr_table indexed by sensor->id), causing out-of-bounds access when sensors with higher IDs (like temperature or pressure sensors) attempt to write this attribute.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement unconditionally registers the st_lsm6dsx_buffer_attrs for all sensor types in the loop (all values of i from 0 to ST_LSM6DSX_ID_MAX). The buffer attributes include the hwfifo_odr sysfs attribute which invokes st_lsm6dsx_hwfifo_odr_store(). This function contains an out-of-bounds array access because it indexes a 2-entry odr_table array using sensor->id, which is valid only for accelerometer (id=0) and gyroscope (id=1). When other sensor types with higher IDs attempt to write to the hwfifo_odr attribute, the function accesses memory beyond the odr_table bounds.

Author: Francesco Lavra <flavra@baylibre.com>

    iio: imu: st_lsm6dsx: Decouple sensor ODR from FIFO batch data rate
    
    The rate at which accelerometer or gyroscope sensor samples are fed
    to the hardware FIFO (batch data rate, or BDR) does not have to
    coincide with the sensor sampling frequency (output data rate, or
    ODR); the only requirement is for the BDR to not be greater than
    the OD
bic_trace_step.reason: The function at line 864 calls `devm_iio_kfifo_buffer_setup_ext()` for ALL sensor types (loop iterates through ST_LSM6DSX_ID_MAX at line 860), passing `st_lsm6dsx_buffer_attrs` which includes the buffer sampling frequency sysfs attribute. However, the underlying `st_lsm6dsx_hwfifo_odr_store()` function only supports accelerometer and gyroscope (indexed 0-1) by accessing a 2-entry `odr_table` array indexed by `sensor->id`. When other sensor types with higher IDs (e.g., temperature sensor with ID > 1) attempt to write this attribute, it causes out-of-bounds array access. The vulnerable construct is present: unconditional attribute registration for all sensor types without filtering, combined with the store function's limited support for only 2 sensor types.
